detail.longDescription: I'm building a browser-based FPS game and I want to include gamepad/xbox controller support. The common method to detect gamepad button presses is to just use polling with requestAnimationFrame : function poll() { let gamepads = navigator.getGamepads(); if (gamepads.length > 0) { let gamepad = gamepads[0]; if (gamepad.buttons[0].pressed) { console.log("Button 'A' pressed!"); } } requestAnimationFrame(poll); } poll(); The problem with this method is that, if there is a large drop in framerate (such as a sudden freeze), the user will be able to press a button once or multiple times, which will go undetected while the freeze happens. This doesn't just happen with low framerates either. It happens even on devices with high framerates. I notice it especially when I spam a button and the script only detects one or two presses. What I'm looking for is a way to detect gamepad button presses as an event listener rather than polling since that would be more accurate. Is there a way to do that?
